extracted.intended_audience: DoD/agency Contracting Officers and study teams involved in OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing/outsourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and appendices adapted from OMB Circular A-76 describing (a) definitions and procedures for competitive sourcing (cost comparisons, MEO reviews, QA surveillance, start date), (b) example commercial activities, and (c) a list of inherently governmental functions not to be outsourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO Performance Review
rubrics_metrics.description: When services are performed in-house as a result of a cost comparison, including those involving an Interservice Support Agreement (ISSA), a formal review and inspection of the Most Efficient Organization (MEO) should be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically conducted following the end of the first full year of performance. Post-MEO Performance Reviews confirm that the MEO has been implemented in accordance with the Transition Plan, establish the MEO’s ability to perform the services of the Performance Work Statement (PWS), and confirm that actual costs are within the estimates contained in the in-house cost estimate. Adjustments may be made for formal mission or scope of work changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Surveillance is the method by which Federal employees will supervise in-house or contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to ensure that required standards of performance are met and that services are delivered in accordance with contract/PWS and cost expectations. (Page text emphasizes surveillance to assure standards and cost control; implement surveillance methods appropriate to the service being performed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Start date' is used in two ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First, it is the date when a cost comparison begins (generally defined as the date that a local Study Team is formed and actual work on the Performance Work Statement, Management Plan, and in-house cost estimate begins). Second, it may refer to the actual date work is scheduled to begin under a contract, as provided in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential Procurement Programs (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferential Procurement Programs are special 'commercial' source programs used in procurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Federal Prison Industries and the workshops administered by the Committee for the Purchase from the Blind and Other Severely Handicapped under the Javits-Wagner-O’Day Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privatization (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Privatization is the process of changing a public entity or enterprise to private control and ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does not include determinations as to whether a support service should be obtained through public or private resources when the Government retains full responsibility and control over the delivery of those services (i.e., outsourcing where government retains responsibility is not 'privatization' in this sense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Commercial Activities (categories and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix B: illustrative list of commercial activities adapted from OMB Circular A-76 that are candidates for performance by commercial sources or for competitive sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories and examples include (not exhaustive): Audiovisual products and services (photography, film/videotape production, microfilming, graphics, distribution, reproduction, facility management, equipment maintenance); Automatic Data Processing (batch processing, time-sharing, programming, systems analysis, keypunching, data entry, systems engineering, equipment installation/maintenance); Food Services (cafeterias, mess halls, vending, ice/water); Health Services (surgical, medical, dental, psychiatric care, hospitalization, outpatient, physical/eye/hearing exams, labs, preventive medicine, dietary, veterinary); Industrial Shops and Services (machine, carpentry, electrical, plumbing, painting, equipment fabrication/repair/calibration, fire protection, custodial, refuse collection); Maintenance/Overhaul/Repair/Testing (aircraft, ships, motor vehicles, combat vehicles, railway systems, electronic equipment, weapons, medical equipment, furniture, industrial plant, photographic equipment, space systems); Management Support Services (advertising/public relations, financial/payroll, debt collection); Manufacturing/Fabrication/Processing/Testing/Packaging (ordnance, clothing/textiles, chemical products, lumber, communications/electronics, rubber/plastic, optical, sheet metal, machined products, construction materials, test equipment); Office/Admin Services (library operations, stenography/transcribing, word processing/data entry, mail/messenger, translation, management information systems, financial/compliance auditing, court reporting, material/supply services); Other Services (laundry/dry cleaning, mapping/charting, architect & engineer services, geological surveys, cataloging, training, specialized utility operation, laboratory testing); Printing & Reproduction; Real Property (design, engineering, construction, maintenance, landscaping, dredging); Security (guard/protective services, security system engineering/installation/maintenance, forensic labs); Special Studies & Analyses (cost-benefit, statistical, scientific data studies, regulatory, defense/education/energy studies, legal/litigation, management studies); Systems Engineering/Installation/Operation/Maintenance/Testing (communications systems, missile ranges, satellite tracking, radar, television systems); Transportation (motor pools, bus service, vehicle operation/maintenance, air/water/land transport of people/cargo, trucking/hauling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of prosecutions and performance of adjudicatory functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The control of prosecutions and performance of adjudicatory functions (other than those relating to arbitration or other methods of alternative dispute resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as inherently governmental — therefore not appropriate for contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command of military forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The command of military forces, especially the leadership of military personnel who are members of the combat, combat support or combat service support role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherently governmental; operational command and leadership responsibilities must remain under government control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of foreign relations and determination of foreign policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of foreign relations and the determination of foreign policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherently governmental responsibility; includes representation and decisions affecting international relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of agency policy (regulatory content/application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of agency policy, such as determining the content and application of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing policy and regulatory content is inherently governmental and should not be delegated to contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Federal program priorities or budget requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of Federal program priorities or budget requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting program priorities and preparing budget requests are governmental functions requiring government decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and control of Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction and control of Federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory and managerial authority over government staff is inherently governmental and must be retained by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and control of intelligence and counter-intelligence operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction and control of intelligence and counter-intelligence operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core national security functions that must remain within government control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection or non-selection of individuals for Federal Government employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection or non-selection of individuals for Federal Government employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about hiring/firing are inherently governmental and should not be performed by contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of position descriptions and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of position descriptions and performance standards for Federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing and approving official job descriptions and performance expectations is an inherently governmental act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of what Government property is to be disposed of and on what terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of what Government property is to be disposed of and on what terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency retains decision authority, though an agency may give contractors authority to dispose of property at prices within specified ranges and subject to reasonable conditions deemed appropriate by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining what supplies or services are to be acquired by the Government
rubrics_metrics.description: In Federal procurement activities with respect to prime contractors: determining what supplies or services are to be acquired by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although an agency may give contractors some authority to acquire supplies at prices within specified ranges and subject to other reasonable conditions, the government must retain the core decision of what to acquire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating as a voting member on any source selection boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating as a voting member on any source selection boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors cannot serve as voting members on source selection boards; such decision-making participation is inherently governmental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of contractual documents defining requirements, incentives, evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of any contractual documents, to include documents defining requirements, incentive plans, and evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final approval of requirements and evaluation criteria is an inherently governmental act and must be done by agency personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarding contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to award government contracts is inherently governmental and must be performed by authorized government officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Administering contracts (including ordering changes in contract performance or contract quantities, taking action based on evaluations of contractor performance, and related contract administration actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core contract administration actions that change scope, quantities, or respond to performance issues are inherently governmental responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminating contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority to terminate government contracts is an inherently governmental decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining whether contract costs are reasonable, allocable, and allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether contract costs are reasonable, allocable, and allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accountability determination is an inherently governmental function; contractors should not make final cost allowability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of FOIA responses requiring judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of agency responses to Freedom of Information Act requests (other than routine responses that do not require the exercise of judgment), and the approval of agency responses to the administrative appeals of denials of Freedom of Information Act requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses that require judgment about release/withholding or appeals must be approved by agency officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of administrative hearings affecting security clearances or personal reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of administrative hearings to determine the eligibility of any person for a security clearance, or involving actions that affect matters of personal reputation or eligibility to participate in Government programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjudicatory decisions are inherently governmental and not delegable to contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of Federal licensing actions and inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of Federal licensing actions and inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government officials must approve licensing decisions and inspections that exercise governmental authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of budget policy, guidance, and suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of budget policy, guidance, and suitability (budget policy and guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting budget policy/guidance is an inherently governmental activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection, control, and disbursement of public funds (with narrow exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection, control, and disbursement of fees, royalties, duties, fines, taxes and other public funds, unless authorized by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exceptions exist (e.g., title 31 U.S.C. 3718 and private collection contractors). Exceptions noted: (a) collection of fees, fines, penalties, costs or other charges from visitors/temporary patrons of facilities where amounts are easily calculated or predetermined and funds can be easily controlled using standard cash management techniques, and (b) routine voucher and invoice examination. Even where limited delegations occur, overall control and accountability remain governmental responsibilities.
